subject: negative factor loadings in nested factor model: optimizer issue?

messages.author: dd77bbde7a69fe72
messages.subject: negative factor loadings in nested factor model: optimizer issue?
parts:
Hi all,

I discovered a couple of times negative factor loadings in my nested factor models that should be positive. I thought it might be an issue with starting values / the optimizer / ... . So I looked systematically at the issue and tried to find an reproducible example.

Here it is: Three correlation matrices as input for a nested factor model with a general factor and one specific factor. All factor loadings should be positive.

library(lavaan)

# data input
mat.1 <- structure(c(1, 0.52, 0.52, 0.52, 0.52, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.52, 1, 0.52, 0.52, 0.52, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.52, 0.52, 1, 0.52, 0.52, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.52,
                     0.52, 0.52, 1, 0.52, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.52, 0.52,
                     0.52, 0.52, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1), .Dim = c(10L, 10L),
                   .Dimnames = list(c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5"),
                                    c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5")))

mat.2 <- structure(c(1, 0.54, 0.54, 0.54, 0.54, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.54, 1, 0.54, 0.54, 0.54, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.54, 0.54, 1, 0.54, 0.54, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.54,
                     0.54, 0.54, 1, 0.54, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.54, 0.54,
                     0.54, 0.54, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1), .Dim = c(10L, 10L),
                   .Dimnames = list(c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5"),
                                    c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5")))

mat.3 <- structure(c(1, 0.56, 0.56, 0.56, 0.56, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.56, 1, 0.56, 0.56, 0.56, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.56, 0.56, 1, 0.56, 0.56, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.56,
                     0.56, 0.56, 1, 0.56, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.56, 0.56,
                     0.56, 0.56, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44, 0.44,
                     0.44, 0.44, 1), .Dim = c(10L, 10L),
                   .Dimnames = list(c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5"),
                                    c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "b1", "b2", "b3", "b4", "b5")))

# CFA
mod.nested.factor <- '
  g =~ a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5 + b1 + b2 + b3 + b4 + b5
  f1 =~ a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5
'

fit.1 <- cfa(mod.nested.factor, sample.cov = mat.1, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.1) # negative factor loadings

fit.2 <- cfa(mod.nested.factor, sample.cov = mat.2, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.2) # positive factor loadings

fit.3 <- cfa(mod.nested.factor, sample.cov = mat.3, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.3) # positive factor loadings

The first model showed negative factor loadings (-0.283) for the specific factor, the other two models showed positive factor loadings. Please note: The pattern is not consistent. Sometimes (after restarting R) some other models has negative factor loadings. I thought providing starting values might solve the issue:

# CFA start values
mod.nested.factor.startvalue <- '
  g =~ a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5 + b1 + b2 + b3 + b4 + b5
  f1 =~ start(.8)*a1 + start(.8)*a2 + start(.8)*a3 + start(.8)*a4 + start(.8)*a5
'

fit.1.startvalue <- cfa(mod.nested.factor.startvalue, sample.cov = mat.1, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.1.startvalue) # positive factor loadings

fit.2.startvalue <- cfa(mod.nested.factor.startvalue, sample.cov = mat.2, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.2.startvalue) # negative factor loadings

fit.3.startvalue <- cfa(mod.nested.factor.startvalue, sample.cov = mat.3, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.3.startvalue) # positive factor loadings

However, it does not really help. In more complex analysis, different starting values (e.g., .8., .9) change the signs of the factor loadings in an unpredictable matter. It helps to introduce model constraints:

# CFA constraints
mod.nested.factor.constraint <- '
  g =~ a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5 + b1 + b2 + b3 + b4 + b5
  f1 =~ c1*a1 + c2*a2 + c3*a3 + c4*a4 + c5*a5

  c1 > 0
  c2 > 0
  c3 > 0
  c4 > 0
  c5 > 0
'

fit.1.constraint <- cfa(mod.nested.factor.constraint, sample.cov = mat.1, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.1.constraint) # positive factor loadings

fit.2.constraint <- cfa(mod.nested.factor.constraint, sample.cov = mat.2, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.2.constraint) # positive factor loadings

fit.3.constraint <- cfa(mod.nested.factor.constraint, sample.cov = mat.3, sample.nobs = 500, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE)
summary(fit.3.constraint) # positive factor loadings

However, that is only a suboptimal solution when you working with real data or more complex models.

Are there any solutions to convince lavaan to use the correct (=positive) factor loadings without constraints or playing around with starting values?

André
(lavaan version: 0.5.20; R version 3.2.4 Revised (2016-03-16 r70336))

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: negative factor loadings in nested factor model: optimizer issue?
parts:
I don't think this phenomenon is specific to lavaan or any of R's optimizers.  The same thing has happened to me in Mplus, and I'm sure it happens in LISREL, EQS, Amos, etc.  When all of the loadings are in the same direction and the factors are uncorrelated, you get the same model-implied covariance matrix if you just switch the signs:

lavInspect(fit.1, "cov.ov")
lavInspect(fit.1.constraint, "cov.ov")

You should get all positive loadings even if you just constrain one of them to be positive.  This phenomenon isn't even specific to bifactor models -- I've seen it happen with regular factor models with simple structure (but switching the sign of factor loadings also switched the sign of that factor's covariance with other factors).  I'm not sure what makes the optimizer search in a different place when the off-diagonal elements in rows/columns 1-5 are < .53 than when they are > .53, and the same thing might not even happen in other software for these specific examples.  But the phenomenon does happen in other software.

If you want to interpret your factor in a specific direction, I don't see why constraining a loading to be positive is suboptimal, but you might also consider posting your question on SEMNET to see if a wider audience has come up with any different solutions.

Terry
